_comment: Public one-sentence descriptions of the designs the checker rejects (site/build.py, "What does not count"), keyed by the stem of the file in tests/<task>/negative/ (`negatives`) or tests/<task>/attacks/ (`attacks`). Every negative and attack of tests/expected.json that the checker rejects needs one; the stage comes from tests/expected.json. The internal notes there are never shown.

negatives.const_nan: Always outputs the canonical quiet NaN.
negatives.div_op: The reference with its division steps replaced by the banned run-time `/` and `%`.
negatives.rm_pin: Adds a rounding-mode input that is never read.
negatives.wide_q: The reference with `q` one bit wider, its top bit always 0.

attacks.dsh_sticky_short: The reference with the denormalizer's sticky test two bits short: wrong on some subnormal results.
attacks.dsh_wrap64: The reference with the denormalizing shift taken modulo 64: right at the scoring format, wrong for exponent widths of 7 and more.
attacks.ew_narrow: The reference with an exponent register that is too narrow when the precision is large: right at the scoring format, wrong elsewhere.
attacks.ftz: The reference flushing subnormal results to zero.
attacks.inc_tie_odd: The reference rounding exact ties to the odd neighbour.
attacks.newton_f_minus2: The Newton reference with two fraction bits fewer in its working precision.
attacks.newton_ge1_const: The Newton reference whose correction always adds 1.
attacks.newton_ni_minus1: The Newton reference with one Newton step fewer: right at small precisions only.
attacks.newton_no_ge2: The Newton reference whose correction stops one short: wrong only where the estimate is two below the quotient, and right on every pair of binary16.
attacks.newton_r0_off: The Newton reference with a wrong constant in its initial reciprocal: right at some precisions only.
attacks.newton_rnz_no2mb: The Newton reference whose sticky bit forgets one remainder: wrong only on rare exact quotients, and right on every pair of binary16.
attacks.newton_rnz_nomb: The Newton reference whose sticky bit forgets the other remainder, taking some exact quotients for inexact ones.
attacks.ovf_late: The reference testing for overflow one step too late, so the all-ones exponent keeps its fraction.
attacks.rr_sticky_dropped: The reference with a sticky bit that ignores the division's last remainder.
attacks.zero_by_zero_inf: The reference returning infinity for ±0 / ±0 instead of NaN.
attacks.srt_qds_t2_d0: The SRT reference with one wrong constant in its digit-selection table: right below precision 5, where the bad table cell is never reached.
attacks.srt_qds_t1_d0: The SRT reference with another wrong selection constant: right below precision 5.
attacks.srt_qds_tm_d7: The SRT reference with a wrong selection constant for negative digits: right below precision 5.
attacks.srt_no_corr: The SRT reference without its final correction, so a negative remainder leaves the quotient one too high.
attacks.srt_drop_carry: The SRT reference with one carry of its carry-save remainder dropped.
attacks.srt_no_cin: The SRT reference that forgets the +1 of a negated divisor multiple.
attacks.srt_sticky_sign: The SRT reference whose sticky bit takes every negative remainder for an exact quotient.
attacks.srt_stages_m1: The SRT reference with one stage, two quotient bits, fewer.
attacks.srt_otfc_um: The SRT reference whose on-the-fly conversion takes one digit's decremented quotient from the wrong register.
attacks.srt_otfc_digit: The SRT reference whose on-the-fly conversion appends the wrong bits for the digit -1.
